I added `habit list --json`. All 8 tests pass, including a new one for the JSON output. I couldn't run the CLI itself: the session's permission settings blocked it, so only the `list()` function underneath has been tested.

**Changes:**
- **`src/commands.js`**: `list()` takes a `{ json }` option. When it's set, it prints an array of `{ name, streak, done }` objects. With no habits it prints `[]` instead of the "No habits yet" message, so scripts can always parse the output.
- **`src/cli.js`**: `list` passes the option on when `--json` appears in its arguments. I also updated the usage text.
- **`test/commands.test.js`**: the new test covers the empty case and a habit with a 2-day streak.
- **`README.md`**: added a line showing `list --json`.

Example output:
```json
[
  {
    "name": "read",
    "streak": 1,
    "done": ["2026-09-27"]
  }
]
```

Two things you might want to change:
- The output includes the raw `done` dates as well as the streak. Drop that field if you only want name and streak.
- The flag only works on `list`. `add` and `done` would treat `--json` as part of the habit name.

To check the CLI yourself, point it at a throwaway file so your real `habits.json` isn't touched:
```sh
HABITS_FILE=/tmp/h.json node src/cli.js add read
HABITS_FILE=/tmp/h.json node src/cli.js done read
HABITS_FILE=/tmp/h.json node src/cli.js list --json
```
